name: Optimizer
description: A process RAM is a sequence of bytes that are indexed from 1 to n . Polycarpus's program contains such instructions as " memset ", that is, the operations of filling memory cells on a segment with some value. The details are: the code only contains m instructions that look like " set13 a_i l_i ". Instruction i fills a continuous memory segment of length l i , starting from cell number a i , (that it cells with numbers a i , a i + 1, ..., a i + l i - 1 ) with values 13. In Polycarpus's code, the optimizer's task is to remove the maximum number of instructions from his code in such a way that the remaining instructions set value 13 in all the memory bytes that got this value from the code before the optimization. Also, the value 13 should be set only in the memory bytes that got this value from the code before the optimization. Your task is to implement the optimizer for such program.
input_specification: The first line contains integers n and m ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10 6 , 1 ≤ m ≤ 2·10 5 ) — the number of bytes (memory cells) and the number of instructions in Polycarpus's code. Then m lines follow, each line contains a pair of integers a i , l i ( 1 ≤ a i ≤ n , 1 ≤ l i ≤ n - a i + 1 ).
output_specification: Print in the first line the sought maximum number of instructions that can be removed from the code. In the second line print the numbers of the instructions. The instructions are numbered from 1 to m in the order they appeared in the input. If there are multiple solutions, print any of them.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 306B — Optimizer [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
